audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on either layer said HOW Nevermove roots. Both layers just say "his E Nevermove" and treat it as a skillshot to dodge.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer." The outward pass does not root — the return does, and the pull follows. That single fact is the whole dodge check the content layer already alludes to, and a reader who steps forward after the wave passes them is walking into it.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, tradeGood, report[3].t, loading, tldr and content spikes[0].text and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension was described only as "his drain mode" with no duration model and no cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text says the form "is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions". So it is not a timed window you wait out — it ends when you leave. That is why burst-and-reset beats dancing, and it is a much better reason than the page gave.
audit.corrected: winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, breakdown.mid and report[5].t now carry the flat 120s and the drain condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Skill/Swain. Four rows disagreed across the layers.
audit.why: Neeko shoves first and pokes before Ravenous Flock ramps, which is the early edge both other sources record; levels 4 through first item genuinely are a dodge check on Nevermove; and two-plus items belongs to the champion whose ult heals through a burst rotation.
audit.corrected: The four disagreeing rows moved onto the agreeing sources, with each moved row's why and rating rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.why: The anti-heal instruction in report[8].t is well founded here — Ravenous Flock's soul fragments heal him, per Riot's own passive text. I named Oblivion Orb rather than leaving "anti-heal" as a placeholder (catalogued defect 7).
audit.corrected: report[8].t now names the item and the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions claims "Swain bypasses stacking resistances (Ravenous Flock) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here."
audit.why: The percentHealth flag on his passive misfires. Riot's text says the fragments "heal him and permanently increase his maximum health" — that is Swain gaining health, not Swain dealing percent-health damage or bypassing resistances. Per the rule that the description outranks a derived flag, I wrote no resistance-bypass claim.
audit.corrected: Nothing written; recorded here and in notes so the flag is not trusted next pass.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit — catalogued defect 3.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension flat 120, Nevermove 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 and Death's Hand falling to 3 seconds at rank 5 are all in the kit, and the last one explains why poking him down does not work late in the level range.
audit.corrected: All three now in the field.

notes: BEST ADD: neither layer said how Nevermove actually works. Riot's text — "It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer" — means the outward pass is harmless and the RETURN is the root, followed by an optional pull. The content layer already framed levels 4-6 as a dodge check without ever telling the reader what to dodge; it now does. SECOND ADD: Demonic Ascension "is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions", so it is not a window you outlast — leaving ends it. That replaces the vague "disengage and reset" line with the reason. CHART: full-layer rows 1, 2, 3 and two-plus items said "Skill" while content win[] and packet.levelChart both said Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Skill/Swain; I moved the four disagreeing rows onto them with matched whys and ratings, and rewrote the three even rows' whys too since they were pure template. FLAG MISFIRE: the percentHealth flag on Ravenous Flock produced a missingInteractions headline claiming Swain "bypasses stacking resistances". Riot's text says the fragments heal him and permanently increase his MAXIMUM HEALTH — that is him gaining health, not percent-health damage — so I wrote no resistance-bypass claim. The anti-heal headline from the same passive IS supported and report[8].t now names Oblivion Orb instead of saying "anti-heal". FABRICATION REMOVED: phases[4].why's "3-second knockup". DIFF FIELD: EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 47.67% win rate over 86 games is defensible, so I left the difficulty block alone here.
